players.product: hyperscale rack-level AC-DC power shelves / server power supplies and modular 800 V DC-DC & AC-DC data-center power products

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 2025 results (CFO Paul Oldham): revenue of $489 million increased 6% sequentially and 18% year over year, at the high end of guidance, on strengthening semiconductor, industrial and medical demand plus another record data center quarter; gross margin 39.7%, up 60 basis points sequentially despite tariffs and factory ramp costs ('if you excluded the impact of tariffs, we are clearly well over 40% gross margin'); operating margin 17.8%; EPS $1.94. Full-year 2025: revenue $1.8 billion, up 21%; gross margin up 240 basis points to 38.7%; operating margin 15.8%; EPS up 73% to $6.41; record operating cash flow of $235 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 revenue $489 million (+6% sequentially, +18% YoY); gross margin 39.7%; operating margin 17.8%; EPS $1.94; 2025 revenue $1.8 billion (+21%); 2025 EPS $6.41 (+73%)

quarterly_data.signal: Data center computing revenue was a record $178 million, up 4% sequentially and 101% year over year, and increased sequentially every quarter of 2025. CEO Steve Kelley: 'Hyperscalers have adopted our customized power solutions in a variety of AI rack applications.' Oldham: 'demand remained very strong, and we were able to quickly adjust to meet changes in product mix within the quarter.' Data center mix grew 'from sort of the low twenties to close to 40% by the time we exited the year', Oldham said further data center growth 'could be some headwind' but 'the margins there continue to approach corporate average', and that new products and manufacturing efficiency should let AE 'largely accommodate that within the sort of plus or minus 50 basis points' of net mix impact it has discussed.
quarterly_data.figure: data center computing revenue $178 million (+4% sequentially, +101% YoY); data center mix close to 40% exiting 2025

quarterly_data.signal: 2026 data center outlook raised: Oldham said 'we are raising our data center revenue growth outlook to more than 30%, up from 25 to 30%'. Kelley: 'Our forecast of over 30% growth this year only comprehends our existing customer base. It does not comprehend any pull-ins of demand from second wave customers.' Q1 data center demand is expected to be similar to Q4 'based on timing of product transitions' as new products are qualified and displace older ones, then to strengthen through the rest of the year on higher demand and the production ramp of new programs; the 2025 data center wins go into volume production in 2026. Second wave cloud and enterprise customers are being engaged 'largely with modified versions of our standard technology platforms' and 'don't require a lot of engineering work on our part', unlike the hyperscalers. Kelley: 'I think there's definitely upside to our number.'
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 data center revenue growth more than 30% (up from 25 to 30%); Q1 data center similar to Q4

quarterly_data.signal: Supply constraints: Kelley said 2025 shipments were shaped by 'various constraints on processors, whether it's GPUs or ASICs or some other type of processor product', which in some cases dictated the number of boxes AE delivered, and that memory is the added constraint in 2026: 'Most of the memory makers have announced that they're sold out. So you've got allocation situations in both processors and memory, which will limit some of the growth we believe in 2026. That's why we're a little conservative.' AE itself has not been limited ('I don't see factory floor space or equipment being constraints for Advanced Energy'); its attention is on 'bill of materials and parts and ICs and discretes', so it is building strategic inventory where it sees supply-chain weaknesses. Kelley added that as 'the contention for processors and memories heats up, I think the hyperscalers have an advantage there', which may impact some second wave customer ramps. Q4 inventory days fell by three days to 125 and inventory turns improved to 2.9 times; inventory is expected to increase to support growth and for strategic supply.

800 V transition: Kelley said AE is 'engaged with multiple marquee customers on 800 volts' and 'fully engaged with our customers, including on a number of 800-volt projects', while developing new technologies and products for next-generation AI data centers with key customers. On content per rack: 'based on our analysis of the market, our total dollar opportunity goes up with 800-volt solutions relative to what we're generating today.' 'For us, rapid change is a good thing because we are technology leaders, and it makes it harder for the other guys to catch up essentially.'

Capacity: in 2025 AE doubled capacity in the Philippines and Mexico, completed the initial fit-up of its new Thailand factory and closed its last China factory. Oldham expects 2026 CapEx 'at or around Q4 levels' (Q4 CapEx was $38 million), enabling over $2.5 billion of revenue-generating capacity within the existing footprint, with the complete Thailand build-out (more than $1 billion of annual revenue-generating capacity) on top; Kelley: 'by the end of next year, I think you're looking at $3.5 billion, assuming we build out Thailand.' Thailand, a half-million-square-foot site and AE's biggest factory, will likely qualify its first products in 2026 so they can ramp 'as soon as Q4 of this year'. The first products are likely data center ('whether it's with our existing hyperscale customers or some new second wave customers, that remains to be seen'), with plasma power and then industrial/medical products to follow. 2025 CapEx was $107 million, or 6% of revenue; longer term, CapEx is expected to revert to around 4% of sales.
quarterly_data.figure: over $2.5 billion revenue-generating capacity in existing footprint; Thailand more than $1 billion; $3.5 billion by the end of next year; Q4 CapEx $38 million; 2025 CapEx $107 million (6% of revenue)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: Q1 2026 revenue approximately $500 million, plus or minus $20 million, with the sequential growth coming primarily from semiconductor (data center and industrial/medical flattish); gross margin in the 39.5% to 40% range; non-GAAP EPS about flat at $1.94, plus or minus 25¢, on 39.7 million shares; tax rate 16 to 17%. Full-year 2026 revenue modeled to grow in the high teens after 21% growth in 2025; gross margin expected over 40% in 2026, with line of sight to the long-term 43% goal (the Thailand factory 'has always been contemplated in our 43% goal'); OpEx rising to a run rate of around $120 million by the end of Q4, 'which probably puts OpEx in the $450 million to $460 million range'. Kelley said AE is confident it can meet or exceed the long-term financial goals presented at its 2024 Analyst Day.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 revenue approximately $500 million, plus or minus $20 million; gross margin 39.5% to 40%; EPS $1.94, plus or minus 25¢; 2026 revenue growth high teens; long-term gross margin 43%; 2026 OpEx $450 million to $460 million

players.product: RF / DC plasma power supplies for etch & deposition tools

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor revenue was $212 million, up 8% from Q3 and ahead of guidance as customer demand strengthened. Oldham: 'At the end of Q3, we expected to be down 2% or 3%. We actually ended up growing 8%. So that's a 10% swing.' Kelley said 'we saw a material change in customer outlooks in Q4', and the upside was not a pull-in: 'The Q1 demand also went up, as did Q2. Our customers have also told us to expect further increases for the second half.' 2025 semiconductor revenue grew 6% to the second-highest level in company history, with new products contributing incremental revenue as design wins moved into early production.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductor revenue $212 million (+8% from Q3); Q4 had been expected down 2% or 3%, a 10% swing

quarterly_data.signal: Semiconductor 2026 outlook: stronger customer forecasts support a strong second half, 'underpinned by downstream investments in advanced logic and memory capacity'. Kelley: 'What we're seeing right now is a surge in demand for advanced logic capacity as well as DRAM capacity. Since we're strong in conductor etch, we expect to see a fair amount of business as those capacity build-outs take place in the coming twelve to twenty-four months.' Other growth factors he listed were a larger installed base of AE boxes, a growing service business and system power: 'over the past few years, we have focused on system power solutions for semi equipment and semi tester companies. We've achieved some success there. Those programs will ramp in 2026.' Asked whether semiconductor could grow toward an analyst-suggested 20% in 2026, Kelley said 'I think it could' but AE is 'not ready to forecast that', citing 'timing issues with the wafer fabs and exactly when the clean room space is available to accommodate new equipment'. He expects customers to hold more safety stock in '26 and '27. Asked about capacity if WFE runs well above an analyst-cited level, Kelley said AE can reallocate internal capacity and that Thailand was originally built as a business continuity factory for semiconductor, to back up the Malaysia operation.
quarterly_data.figure: capacity build-outs over the coming twelve to twenty-four months; system power programs ramp in 2026

quarterly_data.signal: New plasma power products (Everest, EVOS, NavX): Oldham said AE met its 2025 goals for them, 'seeing double-digit millions of revenue for those new products', while they remain 'largely still in the early pilot or early production stage'; 'The ramp of these is largely tied to sub-two-nanometer process ramp', and 2026 revenue is expected to be higher than 2025. Kelley said broad acceptance across a broad customer set is 'setting the company up for structural share gain over the next five years', because customers 'are encountering problems as they go below two nanometers at these advanced nodes' and the products improve throughput and yield. Customers are starting to consider them for non-leading-edge processes, and 'maybe not in '26, but in '27, '28, '29, we're just gonna see the usage of these products multiply'. A number of development projects should convert to wins in 2026, and AE launched 26 new products across its markets in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: new products double-digit millions of revenue in 2025; 26 new product launches in 2025
